qti-assessment-item.title: Diagnose respiratory-swallow phase discoordination (inspiratory post-swallow patterns) in COPD and post-extubation dysphagia on instrumental VFSS/FEES.

qti-item-body.p: Objective (OBJ_1): Diagnose respiratory-swallow phase discoordination (inspiratory post-swallow patterns) in COPD and post-extubation dysphagia on instrumental VFSS/FEES.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: Why does an adult with acute-on-chronic COPD hyperinflation exhibit elevated aspiration risk during sequential thin-liquid cup sips despite intact vocal fold adduction?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Tachypnea and shortened swallow apnea drive post-swallow inspiration, generating negative airway pressure when pharyngeal residue remains near the laryngeal vestibule
Healthy adults always inhale immediately after swallowing to oxygenate the glottis
Bedside absence of overt coughing proves thin liquids are clearing without laryngeal penetration
Thickening all liquids to extremely thick (IDDSI Level 4) automatically eliminates COPD work-of-breathing fatigue and dehydration risk

qti-content-body.p: Verified: Swallow-inspiration phase coupling pulls residual bolus material into the airway during post-swallow inhalation.
Diagnostic rationale: Normative respiratory-swallow patterning is expiratory-swallow-expiratory, which facilitates airway clearance.
Diagnostic rationale: Silent aspiration occurs without reflexive cough, requiring instrumental VFSS or FEES visualization.
Diagnostic rationale: Overly thickened liquids can increase pharyngeal residue, oral effort, respiratory fatigue, and dehydration in COPD patients.

qti-assessment-item.title: Differentiate oropharyngeal biomechanical impairment from pharyngoesophageal motility and gastroesophageal reflux contributors prior to therapy selection.

qti-item-body.p: Objective (OBJ_2): Differentiate oropharyngeal biomechanical impairment from pharyngoesophageal motility and gastroesophageal reflux contributors prior to therapy selection.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: During VFSS, a patient reports a 'food sticking at the sternal notch' sensation, displays normal hyolaryngeal excursion and pharyngeal stripping, but exhibits retrograde bolus flow from the mid-esophagus back toward the cricopharyngeus despite daily omeprazole (Prilosec). What is the SLP's appropriate action?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Prescribe intensive Masako tongue-hold exercises for four weeks without medical referral
Document intact oropharyngeal biomechanics alongside observed esophageal stasis/retrograde flow and refer to gastroenterology for esophageal motility evaluation
Adjust the patient's omeprazole (Prilosec) dosage independently to twice daily
Diagnose a definitive esophageal adenocarcinoma from the lateral fluoroscopy screen

qti-content-body.p: Diagnostic rationale: Pharyngeal strengthening exercises do not treat intra-esophageal stasis or motility disorders and waste clinical resources.
Verified: Patients often localize esophageal retention to the neck/suprasternal region; SLPs document esophageal sweep observations and refer to GI.
Diagnostic rationale: Medication prescribing and dosage changes fall outside SLP scope of practice.
Diagnostic rationale: Medical diagnosis of esophageal pathology belongs to the physician/gastroenterologist; the SLP reports physiological observations and refers.

qti-assessment-item.title: Evaluate standardized speech-language test sensitivity, specificity, likelihood ratios, and dynamic assessment evidence rather than relying on arbitrary SD cutoffs.

qti-item-body.p: Objective (OBJ_3): Evaluate standardized speech-language test sensitivity, specificity, likelihood ratios, and dynamic assessment evidence rather than relying on arbitrary SD cutoffs.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: A school-based SLP administers a standardized language battery whose manual documents 62 percent sensitivity and 91 percent specificity at -1.5 SD, and a bilingual 7-year-old scores -1.2 SD while demonstrating significant narrative microstructure breakdowns and high dynamic-assessment scaffolding needs. How should the SLP interpret these data?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Deny services automatically because the composite standard score is above the district's -1.5 SD cutoff
Recognize that 62 percent sensitivity misses 38 percent of true language disorders, and weight convergent narrative, classroom impact, and dynamic-assessment evidence
Re-administer the exact same norm-referenced subtests the next morning until the score drops below -1.5 SD
Average four unrelated articulation and fluency percentiles into the language composite

qti-content-body.p: Diagnostic rationale: Rigidly applying an insensitive omnibus cutoff violates IDEA multi-source evaluation mandates and misses true impairment.
Verified: Low sensitivity (< 80 percent) produces high false-negative rates; triangulating dynamic assessment and functional language sampling prevents under-identification.
Diagnostic rationale: Immediate re-testing violates test-retest validity and introduces practice effects.
Diagnostic rationale: Averaging distinct construct domains is psychometrically invalid.

qti-item-body.p: Objective (OBJ_3): Evaluate standardized speech-language test sensitivity, specificity, likelihood ratios, and dynamic assessment evidence rather than relying on arbitrary SD cutoffs.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: When appraising a diagnostic speech-language assessment manual, which psychometric benchmark indicates informative diagnostic accuracy for ruling in and ruling out a disorder?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: High internal consistency (Cronbach reliability = 0.90) alone, with zero reported sensitivity or specificity data
Sensitivity and specificity both >= 80 percent at the empirically derived cut score, yielding LR+ >= 3.0 and LR- <= 0.30
Normative sample consisting exclusively of children with no speech or language disorders and zero clinical validation group
Reliance on age-equivalent scores to quantify standard error of measurement

qti-content-body.p: Diagnostic rationale: Reliability does not establish diagnostic classification accuracy between impaired and typical groups.
Verified: Plante & Vance / ASHA diagnostic benchmarks support >= 80 percent sensitivity/specificity and informative positive/negative likelihood ratios.
Diagnostic rationale: Excluding clinical disorder groups from normative samples without a separate clinical sensitivity study cannot establish diagnostic cutoffs.
Diagnostic rationale: Age-equivalent scores are ordinal median estimates with unequal intervals and never measure diagnostic accuracy.
